MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Do NOT copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational assessment questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. Your resume must describe your work and experience, in your own words. To receive credit for your experience, your résumé must clearly state the number of hours worked per week for each position. This information is required to properly evaluate and award specialized experience. Failure to provide adequate detail on hours worked may result in that time not being credited during the qualification review. Please refer to the Required Documents section for detailed guidance on what information your résumé must include. To be considered minimally qualified for this position, you must demonstrate that you have the required proficiency level of competencies and experience for the respective grade level in which you are applying. COMPETENCY REQUIREMENT: Experience must be Information Technology (IT)-related; the experience may be demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (for example, IT certification), as appropriate. You must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the required competencies listed below and must meet or exceed the minimum proficiency level established for each by grade level. For more information, see Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210. You qualify at the GS-15, if you have the following competencies: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 3) Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 3) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) Technical Competence - Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. (Minimum Proficiency Level: 4) AND SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: In addition to meeting the competency requirement listed above, you must have at least one year of specialized experience at the next lower GS-grade level (or equivalent). Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled. Such experience is typically gained in the IT field or through the performance of work where the primary concern is IT. You qualify at the GS-15 grade level, if you have: EXPERIENCE: At least one (1) year of specialized experience at the GS-14 grade level (or equivalent) performing all the following duties: Managing Information Technology (IT) or Operational Technology (OT) programs and personnel to defend cyber infrastructure and architecture assets from known vulnerabilities; Providing advice and guidance to on strategic cybersecurity and information security programs, policies, processes, and systems to reduce cybersecurity risk; AND Coordinating cyber incidents for federal, state, and local government or private sector programs and officials. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualification requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: Integrated Operations Division (IOD) is the hub for staying on top of threats and emerging risks to our nation's critical infrastructure, whether they're of cyber, communications or physical origin. In this position, you will serve as a Regional Chief of Cybersecurity leading a cadre of Cybersecurity IT Specialists performing operational cybersecurity work to defend cyber infrastructure and architecture assets from known vulnerabilities and develop a security risk management plan.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. We achieve these vital missions through a diverse workforce spanning hundreds of occupations. Make an impact; join DHS. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) leads the national effort to defend critical infrastructure against the threats of today, while working with partners across all levels of government and in the private sector to secure against the evolving risks of tomorrow. CISA's mission includes protecting the Federal Government's networks and physical infrastructure, to helping entities in the public and private sectors manage potential risk, to enhancing public safety communications at all levels of government. CISA's multi-faceted mission is home to a wide range of career fields including cybersecurity, program management, business administration, communications, and data science. Joining CISA means being part of the team focused on securing the Nation's physical and cyber infrastructure against threats to public health and safety, economy, and national security; we Defend Today, Secure Tomorrow.
MajorDuties: This announcement is issued under Direct Hire Authority (DHA) to recruit for positions for which there is a critical hiring need. Selectee(s) will receive a career or career-conditional appointment in the competitive service and may be required to serve a one year probationary period. The official title of this position is Supervisory IT Cybersecurity Specialist (INFOSEC) GS-2210-15. Typical work assignments include, but are not limited to: Coordinating partner outreach and support through Federal and State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial (SLTT) government, and critical infrastructure relationships; aligning resources and milestones to DHS/CISA/IOD goals. Analyzing results from subordinate-led engagements to develop multi-regional strategies; and communicates CISA cybersecurity initiatives and capabilities through briefings, conferences, and public speaking. Conducting and overseeing cyber protective visits and strategic cyber risk assessments. Developing cybersecurity operational analysis and planning (e.g., regional annual operations planning). Advising senior leadership on strategic cybersecurity issues and risk reduction.
Details.Education: Education may not be substituted for experience. You must meet the qualification requirements specified in the "Qualifications" section of this announcement.
Details.Requirements: You must be a U.S. citizen. Complete the initial online assessment and USA Hire Assessment, if required. Selective Service - Males born after 12/31/59 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service, see http://www.sss.gov/ All Federal employees are required to participate in Direct Deposit/Electronic Funds Transfer for salary payments. DHS uses E-Verify, an Internet-based system, to confirm the eligibility of all newly hired employees to work in the United States. Learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities. You must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance suitable for Federal employment as determined by a background investigation. This may include a credit check, a review of financial issues, as well as certain criminal offenses and illegal use or possession of drugs. This position may be designated as essential personnel. Essential personnel must be able to serve during continuity of operation events without regard to declarations of liberal leave or government closures due to weather, protests, and acts of terrorism or lack of funding. Failure to report for or remain in this position may result in disciplinary or adverse action in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and regulations (5 U.S.C. 7501-7533 and 5 CFR Part 752, as applicable). This position has been identified as a drug testing designated position (TDP) for purposes of the CISA's Drug-Free Workplace Program. All applicants tentatively selected for this position will be required to submit to a drug test to screen for illicit/illegal drug use prior to receiving a final offer of employment. A final offer of employment is contingent upon a negative drug test result. After appointment, you may be subject to periodic random drug testing. The selectee must possess and maintain a valid state driver's license.
Details.Evaluations: Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), your responses on the application questionnaire, and your responses to all assessments required for this position. This position is being filled using Direct Hire Authority (DHA). Under DHA, applicants are not subject to the traditional competitive rating and ranking process, and veterans' preference does not apply. Applicants who meet the qualification requirements may be considered for selection without being rated or ranked against other applicants. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics): Accountability Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Decisiveness Flexibility Information Management Interpersonal Skills Oral Communication Problem Solving Resilience Teamwork Technical Competence Overstating your qualifications and/or experience in your application materials or application questionnaire may result in your removal from consideration. Interagency/Career Transition Assistance Program (I/CTAP): If you have never worked for the federal government, you are not I/CTAP eligible. View information about I/CTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website. To be considered under I/CTAP, you must be rated eligible based on minimum qualifications for this position. In addition, you must submit the supporting documents listed under the required documents section of this announcement. Structured Resume Review: Subject matter experts (SMEs) will review your resume to determine your technical qualifications for this position based on the required specialized experience. SMEs will not review additional information beyond your resume (e.g., cover letter). Applicants passing the structured resume review will move on to the next phase of the assessment process. To preview the application questionnaire, click here: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13109428

This provides an opportunity for you to highlight your dedication to public service for the hiring manager and agency leadership (or designee(s)). While your responses are not required and will not be scored, we encourage you to thoughtfully address each question. Please provide a response of 200 words or less to each question. You will be asked to certify that you are using your own words and did not use a consultant or artificial intelligence (AI) such as a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT or Copilot.

The USAJOBS database will not allow an applicant to submit an application that includes a resume over two pages. Be clear and specific in describing your job-related qualifications, as HR cannot make assumptions regarding your experience. For qualification determination, you MUST include dates of employment (month and year) and hours worked per week. For Federal civilian service, you MUST include your series and grade. Do NOT include photographs, social media links (e.g., LinkedIn, GitHub), inappropriate content, or other personal or sensitive information such as date of birth, social security number, gender, religious affiliation. IF INCLUDED YOUR RESUME WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. 2. COMPLETE APPLICATION QUESTIONNAIRE AND ONLINE USA HIRE ASSESSMENTS If you are requesting a reasonable accommodation for the USA Hire Assessments, submit a Reasonable Accommodation Request and provide documentation to support your request. 3. OTHER SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS (only submit if applicable): CURRENT OR FORMER FEDERAL CIVILIAN EMPLOYEE: Submit a copy of your most recent SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action which shows the grade, step, tenure (block 24) "1" (Career) or "2" (Career-Conditional), and position occupied (block 34) "1" (Competitive Service). Schedule Policy/Career employees submit a copy of your initial appointment SF-50 and proof of competitive status. Provide proof of permanent appointment if applying based on an Interchange Agreement. If applying for a higher grade, provide a SF-50 which shows the length of time you have been in your current/highest grade or promotion potential held. You may need to provide more than one (1) SF-50, if your SF-50 does not clearly demonstrate that you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Appointment/Conversion, Within-Grade/Range Increases and Promotion actions). NOTE: Pay adjustments and awards are NOT acceptable. VETERAN DOCUMENTATION: Submit a copy of your DD-214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (Member Copy 4 or equivalent). ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: If applying based on eligibility under the Veterans Opportunity to Work (VOW) Act, you must submit certification from the Armed Forces that you will be discharged or released from active duty within 120 days from the date on the certification. This must indicate your dates of active service, rank/grade, expected character of service (i.e., honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e., separation or retirement). NOTE: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If selected, a DD-214 must be provided prior to appointment. 10-POINT VETERANS' PREFERENCE: If claiming 10-point Veterans' Preference, you will need to submit a SF-15 and provide an official document from the Department of Veterans Affairs or from a branch of the Armed Forces certifying your overall compensable service-connected disability rating (NOTE: Your overall percentage must be clearly shown), and/or any other associated documentation based on your preference. INTERAGENCY/CAREER TRANSITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (I/CTAP): Submit a copy of the following: Reduction in Force (RIF) separation notice, notice of proposed removal for failure to relocate, notice of disability annuity termination, or certification from the National Guard Bureau or Military Department that you are eligible for disability retirement; SF-50 "Notification of Personnel Action", documenting your RIF separation, noting your position, grade level, and duty location, and/or Agency certification of inability to place you through reemployment priority list (RPL), etc.; Latest performance appraisal including your rating; AND Any documentation from your agency that shows your current promotion potential. CURRENT OR FORMER POLITICAL SCHEDULE A, SCHEDULE C, NON-CAREER SES OR PRESIDENTIAL APPOINTEE EMPLOYEE: Submit a copy of your applicable SF-50, along with a statement that provides the following information regarding your most recent political appointment: Position title; Type of appointment (Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES, or Presidential Appointee); Agency; AND Beginning and ending dates of appointment.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To meet Minimum Qualifications for this IT Cybersecurity Specialist position you must demonstrate (1) the IT Competencies for the federal 2210 series AND (2) Specialized Experience (or optional education). Your resume must describe your IT-related experience to demonstrate these qualifications. Consideration will be given to paid or unpaid work, as well as relevant assignments or tasks completed as part of your education or training. Your resume must clearly describe the duties you perform(ed) that provide experience in these areas.. IT Competencies relevant to this position: .Attention to Detail: Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service: Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making: Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management: Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills: Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication: Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving: Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork: Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Technical Competence: Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. *********************************************** SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE for GS-09 must have been gained in a federal position at or above GS-07 OR (if your experience is on another federal pay scale OR outside of federal service) by performing duties at a level of responsibility and difficulty equivalent to GS-07. Credit will be given for relevant work or assignments / tasks performed as part of your education or training. Your resume must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities for each position held. Specialized Experience is work that involves following established procedures to support the planning, development, implementation of and/or maintenance of information security programs or policies. If you have this experience, your resume must describe, in your own words, the specific duties you perform that demonstrate it. Reviewers cannot assume you perform duties you don't describe. Your experience should include: Participating in the development of IT security policies and procedures. Participating with risks assessments and helping develop disaster recovery or contingency plans. Participating with collecting, analyzing, and documenting security-related information and recommendations Participating with explaining technical security information and recommendations to different audiences. In lieu of specialized experience, you can meet requirements with a master's degree or at least 2 full academic years of progressively higher graduate-level education leading to a master's (or equivalent) degree. (See EDUCATION) *********************************************** SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE for GS-11 must have been gained in a federal position at or above GS-09 OR (if your experience is on another federal pay scale OR outside of federal service) by performing duties at a level of responsibility and difficulty equivalent to GS-09. Credit will be given for relevant unpaid and/or part-time work. Your resume must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities for each position held. Specialized Experience is work that involves assisting with supporting the planning, development, implementation of and/or maintenance of information security programs or policies. If you have this experience, your resume must describe, in your own words, the specific duties you perform that demonstrate it. Reviewers cannot assume you perform duties you don't describe. Your experience should include: Assisting with the development of IT security policies and procedures. Assisting with risks assessments and helping develop disaster recovery or contingency plans. Assisting with collecting, analyzing, and documenting security-related information and recommendations Assisting with explaining technical security information and recommendations to different audiences. In lieu of specialized experience, you can meet requirements with a Ph.D. or at least 3 full academic years of progressively higher graduate-level education leading to a Ph.D.(or equivalent degree). (See EDUCATION) MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS (Specialized Experience or optional education and IT Competencies) must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Selectees must have (or be able to obtain) and maintain a Top Secret Security Clearance (TS-SCI). NOTES ABOUT THIS CAREER-LADDER POSITION This is a mid-level position leading to the GS-12 full performance level. Assignments are developmental in nature and designed to provide experience and technical competence in the methods, procedures, principles and techniques of the full performance level. The supervisor defines objectives, priorities and deadlines, is available for consultation and assists with unusual situations, problems or studies that do not have clear precedents. Employees consult with higher graded analysts to identify problems and methods of approach, but are expected to perform standard, routine duties independently. The supervisor evaluates reports and other completed work for technical soundness, appropriateness of conclusions or recommendations, consistency and relevance. During this period of training, management broadens assignments to enable the incumbent to eventually perform all the duties of the next higher grade. Consideration for promotion is at the discretion of management and is based on the existence of higher-level work your ability to perform that work, administrative requirements and current agency and/or organizational restrictions. Information on this job series can be found at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/

Details.JobSummary: See QUALIFICATIONS for information about this position. Supports the day-to-day functionality and protection of Social Security Administration information technology systems by developing and implementing cybersecurity programs, policies, procedures and digital tools. See DUTIES for responsibilities.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Do you have a desire to: help SSA manage its Social Security programs? analyze and solve problems? help and advise millions of retired and disabled individuals? work on a team to make a difference in people's lives and your own? Join SSA, one of the Best Places to Work in the Federal Government!
MajorDuties: Ensure the security and integrity of systems, networks and data.
Test and deploy cybersecurity capabilities and software solutions, ensuring their effectiveness in threat detection, incident response, data protection and compliance.
Apply the Risk Management Framework (RMF) to identify, assess and mitigate risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of SSA data and systems.
Work with stakeholders to develop and implement risk mitigation strategies in accordance with federal standards.
Perform risk analysis, access management, security application development and testing, audit support, technology research and implementation.
Consult with customers and stakeholders to evaluate functional requirements, translate them into technical solutions and deliver actionable results to support the agency’s cybersecurity mission.
Communicate the agency’s cybersecurity program, policies and initiatives to internal and external stakeholders, ensuring awareness and understanding of security requirements and best practices.
Details.Education: This position does not have an educational requirement but specific education can be used in lieu of Specialized Experience. DO NOT SUBMIT A DIPLOMA IN LIEU OF A FULL TRANSCRIPT THAT SHOWS THE REQUIRED INFORMATION. TRANSCRIPTS TO SUPPORT EDUCATION IN LIEU OF SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: To support education in lieu of Specialized Experience, your transcript must show your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and may not be usable to demonstrate your "in lieu of Specialized Experience qualifications." FOR GS-09: If you claim a master's degree in lieu of Specialized Experience submit your full transcript showing your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and may not be usable to demonstrate your "in lieu of Specialized Experience qualifications." Your degree must be from an accredited institution in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) or include at least 24 semester hours of coursework in those areas. If you claim a bachelor's degree followed by 2 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) submit the full transcript for your bachelor's degree as well as the transcript that supports your 2 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree. FOR GS-11: If you claim a Ph.D. in lieu of Specialized Experience submit your full transcript showing your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and may not be usable to demonstrate your "in lieu of Specialized Experience qualifications." Your degree must be from an accredited institution in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) or include at least 24 semester hours of coursework in those areas. If you claim 3 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) submit the full transcript for your bachelor's degree as well as the transcript that supports your 3 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree. Unofficial transcripts or screenshots of electronic/web transcripts with the required information will be accepted at the time of application. CHECK YOUR UNOFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT TO CONFIRM IT SHOWS THE REQUIRED INFORMATION. You must upload your transcripts as part of your application. Documents will not be accepted via email or regular mail. Foreign Education: Education completed in colleges or universities outside the United States may be used to meet the education requirement, but you must also provide documentation that the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in a conventional/accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. NOTE: It is your responsibility to acquire and provide Certification of US equivalency as part of your application. For a list of Credential Evaluation Services see: Credential Evaluation Services. If selected, you will be required to provide your official college transcripts prior to the effective date of your appointment.
Details.Evaluations: (1) Eligible applicants will receive a score based on your responses to the experience questions in the online questionnaire. Preview questions here:https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13104378 (2) Using that score, you will be placed into one of three Category Rating groups. Best Qualified: candidates who demonstrate a high level of knowledge, skills and abilities Well Qualified: candidates who demonstrate a satisfactory level of knowledge, skills and abilities Qualified: candidates who demonstrate a minimum level of knowledge, skills and abilities. Veterans' Preference is considered during this part of the evaluation. (3) If you are among the highest-ranking applicants based on your score, your resume (and transcript, if applicable) will be reviewed by HR to determine if you demonstrate the Specialized Experience required for this position. To qualify based on Specialized Experience, your resume must describe duties you perform that meet the specific requirements for this position (see QUALIFICATIONS and REQUIRED DOCUMENTS), as well as duties that demonstrate the following as they relate those requirements. It must be evident that the duties you describe are at the required level. . Duties not clearly described cannot be credited. -- Knowledge of cybersecurity principles -- Ability to apply information system security principles -- Ability to collaborate with stakeholders -- Ability to communicate security standards It is not sufficient to make claims in the questionnaire that are not supported in your resume. Information not specifically stated in your resume cannot be assumed. Information copied or restated from the announcement or rating criteria will not be considered. If this occurs, you may be found ineligible. Affirmative responses to the eligibility questions and experience in the online questionnaire are subject to verification. To qualify based on Optional Education, your resume must provide information about your education and you must provide documentation to support that claim (e.g., transcript or certificate, as appropriate). (See QUALIFICATIONS, EDUCATION and REQUIRED DOCUMENTS.) (4) The highest-ranked applicants who demonstrate the required Specialized Experience will be referred to the hiring manager following Priority Selection procedures and applicable documents will be forwarded for further review. (See Priority Selection below) Your description of your knowledge, skills and abilities is subject to verification by the selecting official. You may be asked to provide specific examples or documentation or to verify a response by a practical demonstration of your claimed ability. PRIORITY SELECTION: Well-Qualified ICTAP/CTAP eligibles will receive the first consideration ONLY IF appropriate supporting documents are provided (see Career Transition AND Required Documents). Qualified Veterans' Preference eligibles will be placed ahead of others in the category for which they are ranked. Qualified preference-eligibles who demonstrate a compensable service-connected disability of at least 10 percent will be placed in the Best Qualified category. See REQUIRED DOCUMENTS for information on how to support these claims.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: BASIC REQUIREMENT: Applicants must have IT-related education and experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below at a proficiency level equivalent to the next lower grade level in federal service. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as meeting 2 of 4 of the following: Lead and manage cybersecurity or IT security projects from planning through execution, including developing project schedules, tracking milestones, allocating technical resources, and evaluating project performance using structured project management or Agile frameworks. Direct or oversee the design, implementation, and optimization of enterprise cyber defense tools, hardware, and software to protect complex network infrastructures and sensitive data systems. Lead technical vulnerability assessments, system scans, and cyber risk analyses across enterprise systems to identify security weaknesses and engineer remediation or mitigation strategies. Evaluate IT systems against formal cybersecurity standards, security control frameworks, and compliance mandates (such as NIST SP 800-53/RMF, ISO 27001, CMMC, or equivalent industry/federal standards) to maintain system authorizations, approve security plans, and remediate compliance deficiencies. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. CTAP/ICTAP candidates: To be considered "well qualified" you must meet all of the requirements as described in this section. You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security and Emergency Response, Department of Energy. As a IT Cybersecurity Specialist (CYBERMGT), you will be a recognized expert in IT Cybersecurity Program Manager, who provides independent cyber security guidance, management services, advice, and recommendations to DOE leadership, officials of other Federal Agencies and DOE stakeholders.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
MajorDuties: The Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER) works to enhance the security and resilience of U.S. critical energy infrastructure to all hazards, mitigate the impacts of disruptive events and risk to the sector overall through preparedness and innovation, and respond to and facilitate recovery from energy disruptions in collaboration with other Federal agencies, the private sector, and State, local, tribal, and territory governments. We are truly honored that DOE has been named America's #1 Best Employer for Veterans in 2023 by Forbes-not only among Government agencies, but among employers across the U.S. We are so proud of this ranking which reflects our commitment to the employment of veterans. As so many veterans at DOE renew their service to our Nation, we are deeply committed to their success and advancement. Veterans shape the future of energy As an IT Cybersecurity Specialist (CYBERMGT), you will: Direct the planning, implementation, and long-term sustainment of Department-wide cybersecurity programs, projects, and strategic initiatives to safeguard enterprise networks and mission systems. Serve as an authoritative technical expert and consultant to senior DOE executives, interagency working groups, and external partners on complex cybersecurity policies, emerging technologies, and risk management. Interpret and implement federal and commercial cybersecurity directives (e.g., NIST, CISA, OMB) to evaluate system compliance, mitigate cyber risk, and resolve intractable IT security issues. Oversee the design, installation, configuration, testing, and administration of dedicated cyber defense hardware, software, and tools to ensure system resilience and operational performance. Lead system vulnerability scans, security assessments, and audit reviews to detect deviations from established baselines and recommend remediation strategies across enterprise platforms. Justify program requirements, develops resource and staffing plans, and determines technical training needs to align cyber capabilities with mission objectives and protect classified information.

Details.Evaluations: This position is announced under a government-wide Direct-Hire Authority (DHA) for IT Cybersecurity Specialist (CYBERMGT) positions in the 2210 series. Under the DHA, applicants who meet the Education and Qualification requirements listed in this announcement will be referred for consideration. Veteran's Preference, category rating, and traditional rating and ranking of applicants do not apply under the DHA process. Appointments made under the DHA are processed as "new" appointments. Current Federal employees may be required to serve a new probationary period (5 CFR 315.802(b). The assessment includes a cut score based on the minimum level of required proficiency in these critical general competencies. You must meet or exceed the cut score to be considered. You will not be considered for the position if you fail to meet the established proficiency threshold or fail to complete the assessment. Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., two-page resume, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire, the result of the USA Hire assessment, and a minimum qualification review. Successful candidates will possess the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities and other characteristics): Accountability Attention to Detail Compliance Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Influencing/Negotiating Information Management Information Systems Security Certification Information Systems/Network Security Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Project Management Reading Comprehension Reasoning Risk Management Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork CTAP/ICTAP Eligible Applicants: To receive selection priority, you must submit the following documentation with your application: Proof of Eligibility: A copy of your agency-issued Reduction in Force (RIF) separation notice, a copy of your separation SF-50 (Notification of Personnel Action) noting transition/displaced status, or other official agency documentation confirming your eligible status. Proof of Performance Rating: A copy of your most recent performance appraisal/rating of record, which must include: Your final rating (must be at least "Fully Successful" or equivalent); and The rating scale/guide (explaining what each level/numeric score means), unless the rating scale is clearly defined on the appraisal document itself. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: READ THIS ENTIRE SECTION TO ENSURE YOU UNDERSTAND THE QUALIFICATION AND APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS POSITION. To meet Minimum Qualifications for this IT Cybersecurity Specialist position, you must: (1) demonstrate eligibility for the Recent Graduates Program, (2) demonstrate the required IT Competencies, (3) demonstrate Specialized Experience and/or optional education AND (4) meet or exceed the cut-off score on the USAHire Assessment (see HOW TO APPLY). (1) ELIGIBILIY To be eligible for the Recent Graduates Program, you must have successfully completed a course of study resulting in a degree (associate's, bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate, vocational or technical) or have successfully completed a qualifying certificate program from an accredited educational institution. Your degree/certification must have been conferred within the 2-year period preceding this announcement (i.e., not prior to November 2024). Veterans who were unable to apply within the 2-year Recent Graduates eligibility period due to military obligations may begin the 2-year eligibility period upon discharge from active duty if supported by a DD-214. The new eligibility period may not extend beyond 6 years from the date a qualifying degree or certificate was conferred. (See REQUIRED DOCUMENTS to ensure you provide appropriate documents.) ONLY APPLICANTS WHO DEMONSTRATE ELIGIBILITY AS A RECENT GRADUATE WILL BE EVALUATED (see transcript requirements under EDUCATION below) (2) IT COMPETENCIES You must demonstrate the following IT Competencies either through work (paid or unpaid) or specific IT-related education or training: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations Reasoning - Identifies rules, principles or relationships that explain facts, data, or other information; analyzes information and makes correct inferences or draws accurate conclusions. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. (3) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE Specialized Experience for this IT Cybersecurity position is the performance of basic IT cyber duties or education/training pertaining to incident monitoring and detection; compliance and audit support; documentation and reporting; system testing coordination and/or user support and access management. GS-07 Specialized Experience must have been gained in a federal position at or above GS-05 OR (if your experience is on another federal pay scale OR outside of federal service) by performing duties at a level of responsibility and difficulty equivalent to GS-05. Credit will be given for relevant unpaid and/or part-time work. Your resume must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities for each position held. Specialized Experience for this GS-07 entry level position can be demonstrated by: -- assisting with diagnosing user needs and resolving entry-level IT incidents, -- demonstrating basic literacy in IT security methods, system protocols and protective requirements and -- gathering facts, analyzing system behavior and handling unscheduled halts or routine system errors. If you have this experience (either from a job or performed as part of your education or training), you must describe, in your own words, the tasks you perform that demonstrate it. Reviewers cannot assume you perform duties you don't describe. In lieu of specialized experience, you can meet requirements with a bachelor's degree that (1) shows Superior Academic Achievement (SAA) or (2) was followed by at least 1 full academic year of graduate level education. (See EDUCATION) GS-09 Specialized Experience must have been gained in a federal position at or above GS-07 OR (if your experience is on another federal pay scale OR outside of federal service) by performing duties at a level of responsibility and difficulty equivalent to GS-07. Credit will be given for relevant unpaid and/or part-time work. Your resume must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities for each position held. Specialized Experience for this GS-09 mid-level IT Cybersecurity position can be demonstrated by: -- performing basic vulnerability scanning and analyzing network traffic alerts; -- implementing basic security controls on systems or networks; -- managing user permissions and implementing multi-factor authentication (MFA); -- assisting with minor system modification and security component analysis; and -- participating in IT security assessments and drafting routine incident and status reports. If you have this experience (either from a job or performed as part of your education or training), you must describe, in your own words, the tasks you perform that demonstrate it. Reviewers cannot assume you perform duties you don't describe. In lieu of specialized experience, you can meet requirements with a master's degree or at least 2 full academic years of progressively higher graduate-level education leading to a master's (or equivalent) degree. (See EDUCATION) (4) USAHIRE ASSESSMENT After you submit your initial application, you will be sent an email (to the email address in your USAJobs Account) pertaining to the USAHire Assessment. The USAHire Assessment is a crucial part of the application for this position and you cannot be considered for this position unless you complete the assessment and meet or exceed the cut-off score set by OPM (see HOW TO APPLY for more information). For more information on OPM's Competency-Based Qualification Standards, visit: Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210 NOTES ABOUT THIS CAREER-LADDER POSITION This is an entry level or mid-level position leading to the GS-12 full performance level. Assignments are developmental in nature and designed to provide experience and technical competence in the methods, procedures, principles and techniques of the full performance level. The supervisor defines objectives, priorities and deadlines, is available for consultation and assists with unusual situations, problems or studies that do not have clear precedents. Employees consult with higher graded analysts to identify problems and methods of approach, but are expected to perform standard, routine duties independently. The supervisor evaluates reports and other completed work for technical soundness, appropriateness of conclusions or recommendations, consistency and relevance. During this period of training, management broadens assignments to enable the incumbent to eventually perform all the duties of the next higher grade. Consideration for promotion is at the discretion of management and is based on the existence of higher-level work your ability to perform that work, administrative requirements and current agency and/or organizational restrictions.

Details.JobSummary: A USAHIRE ASSESSMENT is required as part of your application (see How To Apply). The SSA Recent Graduates Program provides Recent Graduates with entry-level developmental experience and is designed to lead to a career in the federal government. Upon successful completion of the program, you may be non-competitively converted to a term (not to exceed 1-4 years) or permanent appointment.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Do you have a desire to: help SSA manage its Social Security programs? analyze and solve problems? help and advise millions of retired and disabled individuals? work on a team to make a difference in people's lives and your own? Join SSA, one of the Best Places to Work in the Federal Government!
MajorDuties: As a participant in the Recent Graduates Program, you will receive both formal and on-the-job training to develop the required knowledge and skill to successfully perform the duties of the position.

At the full performance level, supports the day-to-day functionality and protection of SSA information technology (IT) systems by developing and implementing cybersecurity programs, policies, procedures and digital tools.
Ensures the security and integrity of systems, networks and data through various methods.

Performs cybersecurity duties in support of cybersecurity operations, incident response, system administration and security, compliance and policy implementation, user support and training, documentation and reporting and continuous improvement.
Details.Education: TRANSCRIPTS ARE REQUIRED TO DEMONSTRATE ELIGIBILITY UNDER THE RECENT GRADUATES PROGRAM. DO NOT SUBMIT A DIPLOMA IN LIEU OF A FULL TRANSCRIPT THAT SHOWS THE REQUIRED INFORMATION. TRANSCRIPTS TO SUPPORT RECENT GRADUATES PROGRAM ELIGIBILITY: submit a copy of your full transcript showing your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. The confer date must be within the previous 2 years. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and cannot be used to demonstrate your eligibility for the Recent Graduates Program. TRANSCRIPTS TO SUPPORT EDUCATION IN LIEU OF SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: this may be the same transcript that supports your Recent Graduates Program eligibility or may be in addition to that transcript. To support education in lieu of Specialized Experience, your transcript must show your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and may not be usable to demonstrate your "in lieu of Specialized Experience qualifications." FOR GS-07: If you claim a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement, in lieu of Specialized Experience, you must submit: (1) a full transcript showing the confer date and final GPA OR (2) a full transcript showing the confer date and official documentation showing your class-ranking OR (3) a full transcript showing the confer date and official documentation showing your National Honor Society Membership. If you claim a bachelor's degree followed by at least 1 academic year of graduate-level education (generally at least 18 graduate-level credits) in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) you must submit a full transcript for your qualifying bachelor's degree in addition to a transcript for your graduate education. FOR GS-09: If you claim a master's degree in lieu of Specialized Experience submit your full transcript showing your name, the name of the school, the program in which you were enrolled and the date your degree was conferred. Transcripts without a confer date cannot be considered to have resulted in a degree and may not be usable to demonstrate your "in lieu of Specialized Experience qualifications." Your degree must be from an accredited institution in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) or include at least 24 semester hours of coursework in those areas. If you claim a bachelor's degree followed by 2 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree in a relevant technology field (such as cybersecurity, computer science, information systems management, engineering, mathematics or operations research) submit the full transcript for your bachelor's degree as well as the transcript that supports your 2 academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's degree. Unofficial transcripts or screenshots of electronic/web transcripts with the required information will be accepted at the time of application. CHECK YOUR UNOFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT TO CONFIRM IT SHOWS THE REQUIRED INFORMATION. You must upload your transcripts as part of your application. Documents will not be accepted via email or regular mail. Foreign Education: Education completed in colleges or universities outside the United States may be used to meet the education requirement, but you must also provide documentation that the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in a conventional/accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. NOTE: It is your responsibility to acquire and provide Certification of US equivalency as part of your application. For a list of Credential Evaluation Services see: Credential Evaluation Services. If selected, you will be required to provide your official college transcripts prior to the effective date of your appointment.
Details.Evaluations: You must complete a USAHire Assessment as part of your application (see HOW TO APPLY for more information). (1) You will receive a score based on your responses to the USAHire Assessment, which will evaluate your knowledge, skills and abilities as they pertain to: Accountability Arithmetic Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Mathematical Reasoning Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork The USAHire Assessment includes a cut-off score based on the minimum level of required proficiency in the critical competencies. You will not be considered for the position if you score below the cut-off score or fail to complete the assessments. (2) HR will review transcripts for applicants who meet or exceed the USAHire cut-off score to determine eligibility for the Recent Graduates Program. (3) Resumes and transcripts for applicants who meet or exceed the USAHire cut-off score and demonstrate eligibility for the Recent Graduates Program will be forwarded to the hiring office for further consideration. The hiring office will review those documents and determine which applicants they want to interview. Remember that your application documents will form the hiring office's first impression of your qualifications. Not all applicants will be interviewed so it's important to be clear and specific about your education, IT Competencies and experience. APPLICANTS WITHOUT SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: It's expected that some applicants may qualify on education alone and may not have relevant work experience, but you must still submit a resume that details your qualifications. For entry level positions, any tasks you performed, for example, during a capstone project, internship or heavy coursework can be considered experience and should be included in your resume.

Individuals with hearing or speech disabilities may use the listed email or 7-1-1 for TTY-based Telecommunications Relay Services to call the listed phone number. Additional Telecommunications Relay Services options are available in each state: https://www.fcc.gov/general/trs-state-and-territories. Notice Concerning Materially False, Fictitious or Fraudulent Statements -- Anything you claim in the occupational questionnaire, or your resume is subject to verification. By submitting your application, you are certifying that any statements you make are true, complete, and correct to the best of your knowledge and belief and are made in good faith. (2) USAHIRE ASSESSMENT After you successfully submit your Initial Application, you will be sent a notification (on-screen and by email) advising if you are required to take the USAHire Assessment. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You must meet the following requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: For the GS-14 grade level, you must have one year (52 full weeks) of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service. Specialized Experience for this position includes: Providing technical advice and guidance on cybersecurity, cyber risk management, or critical infrastructure protection matters for senior leadership; AND Developing, implementing, or evaluating cybersecurity policies, strategies, plans, or risk management initiatives to strengthen organizational or critical infrastructure security and resilience; AND Coordinating cybersecurity activities with internal and external stakeholders to identify and address cyber threats, vulnerabilities, incident response, or resilience issues. The experience may have been gained in either the public, private sector or volunteer service. One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-time work is considered on a prorated basis. To ensure full credit for your work experience, please indicate dates of employment by month/day/year, and indicate number of hours worked per week on your resumé. In addition to meeting specialized experience, individuals must meet proficiency levels in each of the following competencies: Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Decision Making, Information Management, Interpersonal Skills, Oral Communication, Problem Solving, Teamwork, and Technical Competence. A Structured Interview may be used to determine if you meet the required proficiency levels. You will be interviewed about past experience or hypothetical situations. For the required proficiency levels and competency definitions, please see the following link: Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210 TIME-IN-GRADE: In addition to the above requirements, you must meet the following time-in-grade requirement, if applicable: For the GS-14, you must have been at the GS-13 level for 52 weeks. Details.JobSummary: This position is located at Departmental Offices, Domestic Finance - Financial Institutions, Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP). As a Senior Cybersecurity Specialist, you will serve as a senior technical advisor and recognized subject matter expert on cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection matters affecting the financial services sector.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has a distinguished history dating back to the founding of our nation. As the steward of U.S. economic and financial systems, Treasury is a major and influential leader in today's global economy. We have over 80,000 employees across the country and around the world. Come Join the Department of the Treasury and Invest in Tomorrow.
MajorDuties: As a Senior Cybersecurity Specialist, you will: Provide strategic leadership in advancing the office's resilience mission and serves as a senior advisor on cybersecurity and critical infrastructure risks affecting the financial services sector. Serve as a cybersecurity subject matter expert for executive-level committees and working groups comprised of federal and private-sector stakeholders. Independently develops strategic work plans, establishes objectives, directs analytical efforts, builds consensus among diverse stakeholders, and delivers recommendations, policies, and products to senior leadership and parent committees. Develop and oversee Treasury's participation in national cyber incident response activities, cybersecurity information-sharing programs, and critical infrastructure protection initiatives.

During this time, your performance, conduct, and suitability for continued employment will be evaluated. You will not automatically convert to permanent status at the end of the probationary (or trial) period. Your supervisor must affirmatively determine that continued employment is in the best interest of the Federal service. If no certification is made before the probationary (or trial) period ends, your appointment will be terminated. You are encouraged to actively engage with your supervisor, seek feedback, and understand role expectations. Additional guidance and support will be provided during onboarding. Must successfully complete a background investigation. All new hires will be required to comply with federal ethics laws. A review of financial or other interests may be conducted to determine if they create any real or apparent conflict of interests with official Treasury duties. Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment to determine your suitability for Federal employment, at the time requested by the agency. Have your salary sent to a financial institution of your choice by Direct Deposit/Electronic Funds Transfer. If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to do so. MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: IT Cybersecurity Specialist (INFOSEC) - ALTERNATE HIRING AUTHORITY
MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Headquarters Air Force Material Command / Special Security & Cybersecurity Division (A2S)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the quality experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Competency-Based Qualification Standards, Information Technology Management Series, 2210. BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: For all positions individuals must have experience demonstrating each of the following competencies listed below:- Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Decision Making, Information Management, Interpersonal Skills, Oral Communication, Problem Solving, Teamwork and Technical Competence. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Your resume must reflect the quality level of experience which demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for successful job performance required for this position. Examples of creditable experience include: IT experience leading cybersecurity, risk management, and information-assurance programs for complex intelligence systems, platforms, and National Security Systems operating across a geographically dispersed enterprise of multiple locations. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Demonstrative knowledge of- and experience with current industry methods for evaluating, implementing, and disseminating information technology (IT) security assessment, monitoring, detection, and remediation tools and procedures utilizing standards-based concepts and capabilities. 2. Knowledge and understanding of IT server & client technologies (hardware and software) for the Windows, Unix and Linux operating systems, including their vulnerabilities and associated security controls. Understand the threats to IT systems as well as the technologies and tools related to attacking and defending IT systems. 3. Knowledge of Industry leading cybersecurity principles and operational impacts of cybersecurity lapses and vulnerabilities using alerts, advisories, errata, and bulletins. 4. Knowledge of a wide range of security concepts, principles, and practices to review, independently analyze and resolve difficult and complex cybersecurity problems; apply policy direction to contractors and government/military officials, and develop guidance for applying security policy, procedures, techniques, equipment, and methods to a variety of work situations and various levels or degrees of security controls. 5. Skilled in discerning the protection requirements of information systems and networks against system and application security threats and vulnerabilities (e.g., buffer overflow, mobile code, cross-site scripting, Procedural Language/Structured Query Language [PL/SQL] and injections, race conditions, covert channel, replay, return oriented attacks, malicious code, etc.) and required countermeasures. 6. Ability to effectively organize and analyze information, produce authoritative reports, position papers, and briefings that are responsive to the specific needs of commanders and senior management officials; present clear and concise findings; effectively advocate for a position; negotiate complex issues using mature judgment and experience. 7. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing; ability to understand and communicate cloud computing deployment models in private, public, and hybrid environment and the difference between on-premises and off-premises environments. 8. Ability to manage a small staff and carry out all phases of personnel management responsibilities. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate is a seasoned cybersecurity executive, mission partner, and people leader who can direct a blended civilian, contractor, officer, and enlisted workforce in protecting the Nation's most sensitive intelligence information, sources, and methods. This individual will serve as AFMC/A2's principal intelligence information-security advisor and lead cybersecurity oversight for intelligence systems and platforms across the command, including oversight of the HAF-appointed Cross Domain Support Element supporting Air Force Intelligence Community Sensitive Compartmented Information cross-domain solutions. The candidate will be equally capable of resolving difficult technical and policy issues, representing AFMC in senior Air Force, DoD, and Intelligence Community forums, and developing practical risk-informed options that preserve security while enabling commanders and directors to make informed decisions. Success requires sound judgment, enterprise perspective, exceptional written and oral communication, and the confidence to challenge assumptions constructively. Providing senior leaders "decision space" and delivering defensible, mission-enabling solutions in a high-consequence national-security environment are highly sought after attributes of an ideal candidate. Position is designated special-sensitive and requires eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), other intelligence-related Special Sensitive information, or involvement in Top Secret Special Access Programs (SAP) to fully perform the duties and responsibilities of the position. A non-disclosure agreement must be signed. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. Cybersecurity Certification is a condition of employment. This position includes cybersecurity and information assurance (IA) work as a paramount duty requirement. Per DoDM 8140.03, the incumbent of this position must achieve the appropriate IA certificate action within six months of assignment of these duties. A waiver of this six-month requirement may be granted per DoDM 8140.03, C3.2.4.2 or C3.2.4.3. Failure to receive the proper IA certification may result in removal from this position. Certification Required: IAM Level III. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below for IMPORTANT additional information. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the Air Force Materiel Command Chief Intelligence Information Security Officer (CIISO) and as a HAF A/2/6 Delegated Authorizing Official-Representative (DAO) for the Air Force Intelligence Community in support of the delivery and use of National Security Systems (NSS) services for the AF Intelligence Community Information Enterprise.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters Air Force Material Command / Special Security & Cybersecurity Division (A2S)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This job announcement may close at any time - apply now! The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel Systems (DCIPS) position implemented under Section 504, Title V of Public Law 99-569, Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1987, as codified in Sec 1601, Chap 83 of Title 10 United States Code which sets forth Air Force policies and procedures for DCIPS. This position is in the Excepted Service. DoD Components with DCIPS positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 USC, in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 2005, DCIPS Employment and Placement. If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. For additional information on DCIPS, click here
MajorDuties: - Command CIISO and focal point for the administration of the Air Force Materiel Command's (AFMC) ISR Cybersecurity Program. - As an AF IC DAO-R, incumbent's authorization decisions impact the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of AF IC element information resources, and determine if the security and privacy risk from operating a system or using a system, service, or application from an external provider is acceptable. - Lead and coordinate with senior military, civilian, and contract employees to complete highly complex security assessment and authorization activities. - Exercise supervisory personnel management responsibilities.

These competencies are normally attained through one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level of the position being filled but may be obtained through other means. Experience may be paid or unpaid (internships, volunteerism). Experience must be validated through the assessment process, consistent with OPM's skills-based hiring policy. Qualifying specialized experience includes: - Leading risk and vulnerability assessments, such as directing comprehensive risk assessments and vulnerability analyses of enterprise systems, networks, and software to identify systemic weaknesses and inform mitigation strategies. - Building cybersecurity architecture, such as developing long-range system security strategies to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of enterprise systems. - Evaluating cybersecurity programs, such as assessing enterprise cybersecurity programs to identify gaps, ensure compliance with organizational requirements, and recommend improvements to enhance overall program effectiveness. Specialized experience must show demonstrable competencies aligned to the position's job analysis and the IT-2210 standard. These qualifications must be clearly referenced in your resume. Additional information on the qualification requirements is outlined in the OPM Qualifications Standards Handbook of General Schedule Positions. It is available for your review on OPM's Qualifications web site: Information Technology Management Series, 2210 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g. Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Generally, time in Non-Pay status as a federal employee is not creditable towards the specialized experience requirement listed above. All qualification requirements must be met by 11:59 pm (Eastern Time) on 11/11/2026.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Small Business Administration, Office of the Chief Information Officer in Washington, DC. The incumbent serves as an Information Technology (IT) Cybersecurity Specialist for the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA). This vacancy is open to CTAP and ICTAP eligible candidates only. If you are not eligible for one of these you will be made ineligible for consideration for this position.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Chief Information Officer
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. As the federal government's leading advocate for small businesses, we empower job creators with the essential resources and support they need to start, grow, and expand their businesses or recover from a declared disaster. Our services reach communities nationwide through a robust network of SBA field offices and partnerships with both public and private organizations. If you're seeking more than just a job - if you desire purpose, impact, and the chance to contribute to something truly meaningful - this is your opportunity. Small businesses are our nation's backbone, driving innovation, creating jobs, and fueling prosperity. At the SBA, you'll directly help empower these vital businesses and ignite economic growth under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and Administrator Kelly Loeffler. For over 70 years, the SBA has fueled America's small business success by providing crucial access to capital, federal contracts, and expert guidance. Beyond our critical disaster recovery efforts, where we deploy aid and expertise to help communities rebuild, your role will directly contribute to the start, growth, and expansion of businesses nationwide, creating jobs and strengthening the economic fabric of our communities.
MajorDuties: As an IT Cybersecurity Specialist at the GS- 2210-14, some of your typical work assignments may include: Lead risk and vulnerability assessments of enterprise information systems to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and protection needs and support remediation. Provide technical oversight of cybersecurity requirements and implementations, develop long-range security plans, and design enterprise security controls. Evaluate enterprise security programs, assess compliance, identify gaps, and recommend improvements to minimize vulnerabilities and strengthen program effectiveness. Investigate security incidents, develop security resolutions, implement remediation measures, and strengthen authentication and authorization controls.
